technical_hypothesis.primary_training_data_risk: care actions, measurement frequency, transfers and documentation change after clinicians perceive deterioration, creating leakage, treatment-confounding and site-specific sequence patterns

training_data.observation_unit: one patient-time window at an escalation cutoff
training_data.input_data: vital-sign sequences, laboratory timestamps, oxygen and medication changes, ward location, procedures and measurement-quality indicators available before cutoff
training_data.target_or_reward: clinical deterioration within a defined horizon, such as rapid-response activation, unplanned ICU transfer or death; exact operational target requires local governance
training_data.label_source: EHR events, rapid-response records and audited transfers; linkage and consistency are unknown
training_data.prediction_time: before protocol escalation or clinician prioritization
training_data.class_balance: unknown; deterioration events are expected to be uncommon
training_data.historical_coverage: unknown across wards, devices, staffing regimes and patient groups
training_data.train_validation_split: time-based and hospital- or ward-held-out validation with subgroup checks and prospective shadow evaluation
training_data.leakage_risks: post-cutoff measurements, ICU orders, rapid-response documentation, treatment changes and increased observation frequency triggered by clinician concern
training_data.representativeness_risks: hospital size, specialty, age, disability, comorbidity, device, staffing and documentation practices differ materially
training_data.feedback_loop: alerts change measurement frequency, interventions and transfers, altering future labels and sequences
training_data.privacy_and_usage_constraints: sensitive health data require purpose limitation, minimization, access controls, auditability and clinical-safety governance
training_data.fallback_if_data_is_insufficient: use validated NEWS2 or local early-warning scores, protocol thresholds, mandatory reassessment, rapid-response criteria and clinician judgment

portfolio_comparison.reason: clinical deterioration sequence prediction is important but is already a mature early-warning category with validated deterministic scores and commercial or research ML implementations; medication and queue sequences overlap existing protocol, stewardship and access-orchestration cases without a distinct uncovered outcome.

existing_landscape.summary: Adopt validated early-warning protocols and evaluate existing EWS or governed predictive modules locally; do not create a separate generic healthcare sequence opportunity.

research.findings: Brazilian evidence supports NEWS2-based deterioration protocols and a 2025 prospective Brazilian evaluation. Comparative and prospective studies show that learned scores can outperform some conventional scores, but performance varies materially and simple NEWS remains competitive. The category is established rather than a differentiated repository opportunity.

where_ai_enters.human_control: nurses and physicians retain assessment, rapid-response activation, treatment, transfer and discharge decisions
